value.title: Panel config, lens-aware evaluator, and reconcile wiring
value.description: Add the opt-in evaluator.panel config (enabled/lenses/maxConcurrent, off by default) and make runAgentEvaluation lens-aware: when panel.enabled with >=2 lenses, fan out one judge call per lens (bounded by maxConcurrent) and reconcile() the per-lens EvalResults into a single canonical evaluator='panel' EvalResult; otherwise run the existing single judge call byte-identically. The combine logic, programmatic eval, retry loop, and EvaluationRunResult shape are untouched.

successCriteria.description: evaluator.panel exists in EvaluatorSectionSchema as an object { enabled: boolean default false, lenses: z.array(z.string()) default [], maxConcurrent: z.number().int().min(1) default 4 }, mirrored in createDefaultConfig; a schema unit test asserts the defaults and that a config without a panel field still parses (panel resolves to the default).

With panel unset OR enabled=false OR lenses.length<2, runAgentEvaluation makes EXACTLY ONE judge LLM call and returns an EvalResult equivalent to today's single-judge path. A unit test mocks createClient (no real LLM) and asserts the client is invoked exactly once on the off path.

With panel.enabled=true and >=2 lenses, runAgentEvaluation issues one judge call per lens, never exceeding maxConcurrent concurrent calls, and returns reconcile(contractId, round, lensResults, timestamp) — a canonical EvalResult with evaluator='panel'. A unit test with a mocked client asserts call-count == lenses.length and peak concurrency <= maxConcurrent.

A 2-pass / 2-fail lens panel reconciles to passed=false (fail-closed), and the reconciled agentResult flows unchanged into runEvaluatorAgent's combine (passed = programmaticEval.passed && agentResult.passed). A unit test drives the mocked client to return 2 pass + 2 fail lens verdicts and asserts the final EvaluationRunResult.passed is false.
npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, and npx eslint src/ exit 0; the full vitest suite stays green with no new failures beyond the documented flaky tool-count baseline.

nonGoals: Do not add the built-in lens prompt catalog or per-lens telemetry — that is sprint 2 (a single inline lens-focus string is enough this sprint).
Do not change the programmatic evaluators, the combine logic, the retry loop, or the EvaluationRunResult shape.
Do not modify src/orchestrator/workflow/reconciler.ts — reuse reconcile() as-is.
Do not touch the workflow engine, .claude/workflows, agents/*.md, or providers/types.ts.
Do not invoke any real LLM in tests — mock createClient.
stopConditions: Stop when the off path is a single judge call, the on path fans out + reconciles with bounded concurrency, and typecheck/build/lint/tests are green.

Stop when changes are confined to src/config/schema.ts (+ defaults.ts if its literal needs the field), src/orchestrator/evaluator-agent.ts, and a new evaluator-agent.test.ts (plus schema.test.ts additions).
value.definitionOfDone: evaluator.panel is a validated opt-in config defaulting to off; runAgentEvaluation runs the existing single judge call when off (byte-identical, proven by a client-mocked single-call test) and fans out >=2 lenses bounded by maxConcurrent then reconcile()s into one evaluator='panel' EvalResult when on; a 2-2 tie fails closed and flows through the unchanged combine; typecheck/build/lint and the full suite are green.
assumptions: runAgentEvaluation (src/orchestrator/evaluator-agent.ts:134) builds the judge prompt and calls createClient; a lens is injected as a focus block into that prompt.
reconcile's sprintId/round args do not affect output, so contract.contractId and an iteration/round number (or 1) are safe to pass.
createClient can be mocked via vi.mock to avoid real LLM calls; the handoff carries the contract + iteration.
value.evaluatorNotes: Confirm EvaluatorSectionSchema.panel defaults (enabled false, lenses [], maxConcurrent 4) and that a config without panel parses. Read runAgentEvaluation: confirm the off path (panel off / <2 lenses) calls the judge exactly once and the lens-less prompt is unchanged from before (diff the prompt assembly — no lens text when lens is undefined). Confirm the on path maps lenses → runSingleLensEval and calls reconcile() from src/orchestrator/workflow/reconciler.ts (not a reimplementation). Run the new evaluator-agent.test.ts: verify the single-call off-path assertion, the call-count==lenses.length on-path assertion, the peak-concurrency<=maxConcurrent assertion (inspect how the mock counts concurrency), and the 2-2 tie → EvaluationRunResult.passed=false assertion. Confirm createClient is mocked (no real LLM/network). Run npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, npx eslint src/ (exit 0), and the full npx vitest run (tolerate only the flaky tool-count baseline). Confirm git diff is confined to schema.ts/defaults.ts, evaluator-agent.ts, evaluator-agent.test.ts, schema.test.ts; reconciler.ts and the combine logic unchanged.

value.title: Lens prompt catalog and per-lens verdict telemetry
value.description: Add a built-in lens prompt catalog (correctness, security, regression, quality) that maps a lens name to a focused prompt fragment, with a graceful generic fallback for custom lens strings, and surface each lens's pass/fail verdict via the existing telemetry/history so a panel failure is attributable to a specific lens. Polish on top of sprint 1; the off-by-default guarantee and fan-out bounding remain intact.

successCriteria.description: A new module (e.g. src/orchestrator/eval-lenses.ts) exports a lens catalog resolving 'correctness','security','regression','quality' to DISTINCT non-empty focus prompt fragments, plus a resolver that returns a generic focus for any unknown custom lens string without throwing. A unit test asserts the four built-ins are distinct and that an unknown lens returns the generic fallback.

runAgentEvaluation uses the catalog to build each lens's focus block (replacing the inline string from sprint 1). With the catalog wired, the off path (panel disabled / <2 lenses) STILL makes exactly one judge call with no lens focus — proven by the sprint-1 off-path test staying green.

When the panel runs, each lens's verdict (lens name + passed) is emitted via the existing emit() telemetry and/or appendHistory, attributable by lens name. A unit test (telemetry/history spy or temp .bober) asserts one verdict record per lens with the correct lens name and pass/fail.
Fan-out bounding (peak concurrency <= maxConcurrent) and the off-by-default single-call guarantee are covered by tests that remain green after the catalog + telemetry changes.
npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, and npx eslint src/ exit 0; the full vitest suite stays green with no new failures beyond the documented flaky tool-count baseline.

nonGoals: Do not change the reconcile semantics or the combine logic.
Do not add lens weighting or non-majority voting.
Do not emit telemetry on the off path beyond what the evaluator already emits today.
Do not touch the workflow engine, .claude/workflows, agents/*.md, or providers/types.ts.
stopConditions: Stop when the catalog resolves the four built-ins + generic fallback, per-lens verdicts are emitted, all guarantees hold, and typecheck/build/lint/tests are green.
Stop when changes are confined to src/orchestrator/eval-lenses.ts (+ its test), src/orchestrator/evaluator-agent.ts, and the evaluator-agent test.
value.definitionOfDone: A built-in lens catalog maps correctness/security/regression/quality to distinct focus fragments with a generic fallback for custom lenses; runAgentEvaluation uses it; each lens's verdict is emitted to telemetry/history attributable by name; the off-by-default single-call guarantee and maxConcurrent bounding still hold; typecheck/build/lint and the full suite are green.
assumptions: emit() (src/telemetry/emit.ts:69) is the telemetry entry point and is fire-and-forget; appendHistory is available for a durable per-lens record if telemetry is disabled.
The reconciler already returns lensVerdicts / the per-lens EvalResult[] is available in runAgentEvaluation before reconcile, so emitting per-lens verdicts needs no reducer change.
Custom (non-catalog) lens strings are valid and should produce a generic focus, not an error.
value.generatorNotes: Create src/orchestrator/eval-lenses.ts exporting a catalog, e.g. `const LENS_CATALOG: Record<string,string> = { correctness: '...focus on whether the implementation actually satisfies each success criterion...', security: '...focus on injection, auth, secret handling, unsafe input...', regression: '...focus on whether previously working behavior still works / pre-existing tests...', quality: '...focus on principles violations, dead code, naming, smells...' }` and `export function resolveLensFocus(lens: string): string` returning the catalog entry or a generic `Evaluate specifically through the '${lens}' lens.` fallback. Keep fragments distinct and non-empty. In src/orchestrator/evaluator-agent.ts: replace the sprint-1 inline lens string with resolveLensFocus(lens) in runSingleLensEval. After running the lenses and BEFORE/AFTER reconcile, iterate the per-lens EvalResult[] and emit each: `void emit(projectRoot, config, 'eval-lens-verdict', { contractId, lens, passed: r.passed })` (follow the existing emit call sites in evaluator-agent.ts / pipeline.ts for event-name + payload conventions; if 'eval-lens-verdict' must be a known event type, either reuse an existing generic event or add the minimal event-name plumbing — keep it consistent with how emit is already used). Only emit on the PANEL path (>=2 lenses), never on the off path. If emit's event enum is closed and adding a value is out of scope, fall back to appendHistory with an event the HistoryEntrySchema accepts (check src/state/history.ts event enum) — prefer the lowest-friction option that the schema allows without broad changes. Create src/orchestrator/eval-lenses.test.ts: assert the 4 built-ins are distinct + non-empty and an unknown lens returns the generic fallback. Extend evaluator-agent.test.ts: assert per-lens verdict emission (spy on emit or read temp history) with correct lens names + pass/fail, and that the off path still emits no per-lens verdicts and makes one call. Use import type, ESM .js specifiers, unicode section headers. Conventional commit: bober(sprint-2): add lens prompt catalog + per-lens verdict telemetry.
value.evaluatorNotes: Confirm eval-lenses.ts catalog: correctness/security/regression/quality map to distinct non-empty fragments; resolveLensFocus('made-up') returns the generic fallback (no throw). Confirm runAgentEvaluation uses resolveLensFocus and that the off path still makes exactly one call with NO lens focus (sprint-1 off-path test green). Verify per-lens verdict emission: spy on emit() (or inspect temp .bober history/telemetry) and assert one record per lens with the lens name + correct passed flag, and that NO per-lens verdicts are emitted on the off path. Confirm whichever emit/appendHistory path was used validates against the existing schema (no schema-breaking event). Run the fan-out bounding test (peak concurrency <= maxConcurrent) and the off-by-default single-call test — both green. Run npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, npx eslint src/ (exit 0) and the full npx vitest run (tolerate only the flaky tool-count baseline). Confirm git diff confined to eval-lenses.ts(+test) and evaluator-agent.ts(+test); reconciler.ts, combine logic, and the event/history schemas unchanged (or minimally + validly extended).
